source.title: CASTLE: Regularization via Auxiliary Causal Graph Discovery
source.authors: Trent Kyono; Yao Zhang; M. van der Schaar

record.tranche_reason: The study compares dropout regularization with an early-stopping baseline on held-out data, using different datasets and metrics from the cited dropout claim. It does not test memorization of random labels or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: Dropout benchmark results are included because the study reports held-out metrics for dropout rates 0.2 and 0.5 alongside a baseline. CASTLE-versus-other-regularizer rankings and results cited from prior work are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The classification benchmarks compare dropout with an otherwise matched dropout-free, early-stopped network on new tabular datasets. Their held-out AUROC results bear on V6's classification-generalization component. Regression MSE results fall outside V6's stated classifier scope. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that CASTLE improves generalization over benchmark regularizers on synthetic and real datasets, claim robustness to feature dimensionality and unrelated noise variables, and state that it never degrades performance in their experiments. They do not make a separate empirical conclusion about dropout's general benefit.
record.recipe_differences: Tests dropout as one benchmark regularizer in supervised regression and classification datasets; no random-label memorization, width sweep, image-network comparison, or claim-specific measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and dropout rate are associated with different held-out results.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout changes held-out MSE on real and nonlinear synthetic regression tasks, with benefits and penalties varying by dataset and dropout rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can improve regression generalization, with effects dependent on dataset and dropout rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports dropout MSE on linear synthetic regression but supplies no dropout-free baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Comparing dropout with other regularizers on linear synthetic regression does not establish whether adding dropout improves generalization.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems 2020 (34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: The paper reports predictive test metrics, not training-to-test gaps. Baseline is early stopping, so it is not a direct no-dropout-only comparison. Table 5 appears inconsistent with Table 3 for some values; the source text's table flattening makes some Appendix Table 5 row assignments uncertain. No explicit small-training-set dropout analysis is reported.
record.rows_left_out: None; the reported dropout rows are included. Appendix Table 5 duplicates some Table 3 results and has apparent conflicting FB entries; retained the table values but marked the uncertainty in notes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning dependence; Adam alone is used.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

Convolutional classifiers; direct classification-error measurements; a controlled training-set-size comparison establishing the very-small-set exception; training-performance evidence of underfitting from excessive dropout; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with image augmentation.
Empirical ranking of generalization gaps by magnitude-aware sharpness versus alternative measures. The theoretical perturbation argument does not test this correlation.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: MAGGIC classification: baseline AUROC 0.644 ± 0.109; dropout 0.2 gives 0.628 ± 0.081 and dropout 0.5 gives 0.679 ± 0.090. Add both comparisons; rows_left_out incorrectly says all dropout results are included.

record.verdict_notes: All benchmarks use validation-based early stopping, identical initial weights, Adam at learning rate 0.001, and at most 200 epochs. Thus early stopping is shared rather than an alternative treatment confounding dropout. Reported ± values are standard deviations across folds, not significance tests. Table 5's FB values align clearly with Table 3; the genuine table discrepancy concerns BC classification dropout 0.2. Duplicate rows should be merged. AUROC is treated as evidence about classifier generalization, with its distinction from classification error made explicit.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
CNNs; very small training sets as a distinct regime; dropout combined with removing weight decay; whether excessive dropout causes underfitting.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring the resulting accuracy change.
